The assignment layer may automate **resource selection/binding**, but it must not inherit Mission-planning authority from Cognition. Phase 7 Cognition must derive the exact availability/capability/preference policy from current Worker contracts and real provider evidence rather than treating the illustrative flow above as a fixed algorithm.

### Current durable PHASE MISSION PLAN — 2026-09-15

**Phase:** Mission Work Phase 7 — Web AI Session Pool and automatic Mission assignment.

**Historical goal:** prove that once Cognition has already authorized a Mission and supplied bounded execution requirements/preferences, Nimora can mechanically discover current Worker resources, reject inadmissible resources, select one deterministic admissible resource, lazily create/bind a disposable WorkerSession to that exact Mission, and later replace a failed Worker for the **same unfinished Mission** without turning assignment into Mission planning, reusing unrelated provider conversations, or converting transport uncertainty into retry authority.

**Current repository Reality:** Phase 0–6 are independently closed on `main` at `79ab464acd0eac9eb623e2f6df2a1276088ece19`; the intentional Phase 1–6 dirty tree is preserved. Dynamic package discovery currently exposes 39 `test-shuncode-*` suites. `WorkerDescriptor` already exposes `id / provider / kind / availability / models / capabilities`; `WorkerSessionManager` owns adapter registration, descriptor refresh, explicit `createSession(workerId, ...)`, Task binding, send/health/retirement and provider-native lifecycle barriers, but contains no Worker chooser, ranking policy, assignment queue or provider/model scheduler. Focused current-baseline runs of `test-shuncode-worker-session-manager`, `test-shuncode-webmcp-command-transport`, `test-shuncode-web-worker-stack`, `test-shuncode-context-handoff`, `test-shuncode-mission-coordinator-live` and `test-shuncode-project-mission` all pass.

Production extension composition currently registers exactly **one** Web Worker definition into its `WorkerSessionManager`: `nimora.web-worker` backed by `WebMcpCommandTransport`. `ApiWorkerAdapter` and `AgentHostWorkerAdapter` exist as real provider-neutral Worker adapters in source/tests but are not registered into that production manager, so Phase 7 must not count them as already-available production assignment resources. The Web transport descriptor itself is also one dynamic definition: `webmcp.integrated-browser`, `site = dynamic`, currently reporting transport-loaded availability rather than page/provider-specific readiness.

The real WebMCP substrate already supports multiple shared Integrated Browser pages, but current `_shuncode.webMcp.workerConnect` calls `getOrShareCurrentBrowserPage()` and selects the visible shared page or last shared page before injection. Only **after** connect does the WorkerSession reveal exact `pageId`, page-session id, site, origin and href. The page runtime currently identifies `deepseek` specially and all other supported pages as `generic`; ChatGPT hosts are intentionally native-MCP bypass pages. Therefore repository Reality does **not** currently expose two independently assignable Web providers as two `WorkerDescriptor`s, and it would be false to implement Phase 7 by merely sorting `WorkerSessionManager.listWorkers()` or by pretending two Web definitions already exist. The canonical WebMCP path has concrete DeepSeek evidence; a second real Web provider must be demonstrated during Practice rather than inferred from the generic adapter.

**Verified upstream invariants:** Project persists while Missions finish; WorkerSession is replaceable compute rather than Mission identity; one Mission may have sequential replacement Workers; Mission completion retires its Worker history; unrelated completed Missions must not silently share one disposable provider conversation; Project/Mission continuity comes from durable Task/Project/collaboration facts and bounded Context Handoff, not provider transcript inheritance. Cognition owns Mission meaning/decomposition/semantic completion. The Phase 6 Coordinator executes/transports exact Cognition-authored commands and consumes exact `managedSessionId`; it does not register/create/select/rank Workers. Capability execution and result delivery are distinct, and UNKNOWN transport/delivery never authorizes blind re-execution. `TaskRuntime` remains Mission work/lifecycle owner; `WorkerSessionManager` remains active Worker lifecycle/router owner.

**Worker resource model:** distinguish three identities instead of overloading `workerId`:

1. **Worker definition identity** — existing `WorkerDescriptor.id`; identifies one registered adapter/runtime definition such as `nimora.web-worker`. It is stable enough for Manager registration/routing, but for a dynamic Web adapter it is not a concrete page/provider resource.
2. **Assignment candidate identity** — a bounded, reconstructible resource observation used only while choosing a Worker. A candidate carries provider-neutral selection facts: `candidateId`, `workerId`, provider identity, kind, availability/health observation, models and implemented Worker capabilities. Adapter/resource-specific locators stay opaque to the selector and are materialized by a trusted candidate source into session options. Candidate identity is **not** Mission identity, Project memory or a provider transcript id.
3. **WorkerSession identity** — existing exact `managedSessionId` plus provider-native `workerId + adapterSessionId`; created only after candidate selection and still owned by `WorkerSessionManager`/Task binding.

For ordinary adapters a candidate may correspond one-to-one with a Worker definition. For the current dynamic Web adapter, multiple shared pages must be exposed as multiple resource candidates **under the same `nimora.web-worker` definition**. This avoids changing stable Worker id semantics merely to model current pages. Web candidate discovery may expose normalized site/provider/origin/readiness metadata, but page ids, DOM probes, selectors, injection details and page-session tokens remain WebMCP/transport-owned and must not leak into generic assignment policy.

**Mission execution-requirement model:** Phase 7 v1 uses an explicit Cognition/host-authored **bounded Assignment Request**, not new fields in `TaskMissionMetadata`. The request binds the exact Project/root/Mission scope and contains only resource-selection information required to choose an executor. Repository evidence does not currently justify durable Mission metadata for provider/model/cost/latency policy, and changing immutable Mission identity metadata would incorrectly conflate Mission meaning with replaceable compute. If later restart evidence proves that some assignment intent must survive independently of Cognition/host re-issuance, Practice must return `PROBLEM + EVIDENCE` before introducing the smallest immutable durable fact; do not silently create an assignment journal.

The v1 request should support a small provider-neutral hard-constraint set such as allowed/forbidden Worker kinds/providers, exact required model when supplied, and required already-advertised Worker capabilities. Privacy/local-only intent is represented as a hard resource constraint (for example local kind only), not inferred from semantic task text. A small soft-preference set may order explicitly preferred providers/models. Cost/latency optimization is **not** a v1 selector input because current `WorkerDescriptor` has no stable typed cost/latency contract; Phase 7 must not invent scores from labels/extensions.

**Hard constraints vs preferences:** hard constraints are fail-closed eligibility rules and can never be silently overridden for availability. “Only X”, “do not use X”, exact model requirements, local-only/privacy restrictions and required implemented capability flags are hard. Soft preferences affect ordering only after hard filtering, such as “prefer X if available”. The request author—not the selector—decides whether user language means hard or soft. If no candidate satisfies hard constraints, assignment returns an explicit no-admissible-resource result/error rather than weakening them. Deterministic tie-breaking after explicit preference ranking uses stable candidate identity; the selector does not infer model quality or task difficulty.

**Availability / health semantics:** `WorkerDescriptor.availability` is an observation/snapshot, not permanent truth. The current Web descriptor proves why: it reports `available` when the command transport is loaded even if no usable shared AI page has been selected. Candidate discovery therefore supplies resource-level observations, and the candidate selected for creation must be refreshed/revalidated as close as practical to session creation. V1 automatic fresh assignment admits only candidates observed as definition/resource `available` and health `healthy`; `unavailable/offline` are ineligible and `degraded` is **not automatically selected**. This conservative policy avoids silently trading reliability/user expectations for availability. If product requirements later demand degraded automatic fallback, that is a separately reviewable policy decision rather than an implicit ranking tweak.

Selection and creation are necessarily racy: a candidate may disappear after observation. A create/connect failure **before any Worker turn has been admitted** may move to the next still-admissible candidate only when the failed attempt's lifecycle/binding outcome is known and cleaned up through existing Manager semantics. Persistence/ownership uncertainty must be resolved by rereading durable Task state or returned as UNKNOWN; it must not cause speculative creation of additional sessions. Once a Worker turn has started, replacement and replay are separate questions.

**Selection ownership / smallest seam:** add one small Nimora-owned **stateless/reconstructible Mission Worker assignment service** above `WorkerSessionManager`, plus a narrow provider-neutral **candidate-source seam**. Naming is not authoritative, but the responsibility is: candidate sources observe resources and materialize exact adapter session options; the assignment service validates exact Mission scope, filters hard constraints, obtains fresh candidate health, applies explicit soft preference ordering plus deterministic tie-break, then calls the existing Manager with an exact `workerId + options + missionId`. The Manager remains the only active session create/bind/route/retire owner. The assignment service owns no Task state, provider transcript, durable queue, workflow schedule or semantic Mission decision.

The generic candidate contract must not require Web concepts. A candidate source may internally retain an opaque locator needed to materialize session options for an exact candidate. For WebMCP that locator can resolve to an exact shared page in the transport layer; generic assignment code sees only candidate/provider/kind/model/capability/availability facts. This avoids extending every Worker adapter with web-specific page discovery while still allowing future API/local/AgentHost candidate sources to use the same assignment contract.

**Assignment lifecycle:** `Cognition-authored Mission + bounded Assignment Request → exact Mission/Project/root validation → candidate observation → hard filtering → fresh health/readiness check → explicit-preference ranking → deterministic candidate selection → Manager.createSession(exact workerId, candidate-materialized options, exact missionId) → durable TaskWorkerAttached via existing binding owner → return exact Assignment Result containing selected candidate identity + managedSessionId`. The Assignment Result is routing output, not a second durable state store. An automatically managed Mission should have at most one current Phase-7 assignment at a time; concurrent initial assignment for the same Mission must be serialized/rechecked so two calls cannot accidentally publish multiple live sessions. Existing manually-created multiple sessions must cause fail-closed ambiguity rather than silent takeover.

**Session-pool semantics:** in Phase 7, “pool” means a **current candidate/resource inventory**, not a stockpile of long-lived model conversations. Default policy is lazy session creation after selection. No cross-Mission provider conversation reuse, no global prewarmed transcript pool and no requirement to keep permanent provider sessions alive. Existing sessions may only be reused when already owned by the **same unfinished Mission** and proven compatible/healthy under the exact request; otherwise create a fresh disposable session. Prewarming is out of scope unless later evidence demonstrates a bounded need without violating one-Mission ownership.

**One-Mission session rule:** every disposable WorkerSession created by Phase 7 for Mission Work is bound to exactly one Mission for its useful lifetime. It may execute multiple turns for that same unfinished Mission. Mission completion/retirement makes that exact provider-native identity durably dead under existing Phase 2 rules. `Mission A completed → silently bind its provider conversation to Mission B` is prohibited. Replacement Worker B for the **same** unfinished Mission M is legal and does not create Mission M2.

**Replacement model:** assignment never equates Worker death with Mission death. For an unfinished Mission M, a known unusable Worker A may be retired through existing Worker lifecycle authority; the durable Mission remains active; a fresh explicit/reconstructible Assignment Request is evaluated; Worker B is selected/bound to the **same taskId/Mission id**; `buildRenderedContextHandoff()` plus current durable Project/Mission/collaboration/execution facts reconstruct bounded context targeted to B. Old provider transcript/session identity is not required. Page refresh or page-session generation change is a Worker resource failure/replacement event, not a reason to create a new Mission.

**Failure / UNKNOWN model:** classify resource failure before deciding replacement action. (a) unavailable before create or fresh-health failure: safe to reject that candidate and consider another; (b) create/connect failure with known no binding/no turn: cleanly fail that candidate and consider another; (c) create succeeds but Task binding fails: rely on Manager cleanup, then reread durable state before any retry if persistence outcome is uncertain; (d) Worker dies before first send: retire/replace is safe because no Mission input was admitted; (e) known terminal failure after a turn: Worker replacement may be allowed for **future newly authorized input**, but does not by itself authorize replay of that failed input; (f) any execution/delivery UNKNOWN, pending capability delivery or ambiguous side effect: replacement may restore future compute only after the current send lease/ownership boundary is settled, and the assignment layer must never resend the old input automatically; (g) rate limit/degraded health/page-session loss: resource observation may make A inadmissible and allow later replacement, but retry of model/tool work still needs the normal Cognition/Coordinator explicit route; (h) finalized/finalizing Mission: no new assignment or replacement is admissible.

**Coordinator integration:** preserve Phase 6 unchanged where possible. Phase 7 resolves the resource **before** a Phase 6 delivery command needs an exact target: `Cognition-authored Mission + Assignment Request → assignment seam selects/creates/binds → returns exact managedSessionId → existing Phase 6 Coordinator command contains/executes that exact managedSessionId`. The Coordinator may transport the already-authorized route but does not list candidates, rank providers, infer requirements or decide fallback. This preserves the verified exact-command schema rather than weakening `managedSessionId` back into a fuzzy selector expression.

**Web-first real E2E strategy:** first add explicit WebMCP resource discovery/selection below `WebWorkerAdapter` so all currently shared admissible pages can be observed without starting a model turn and an exact selected page can be connected. The generic assignment service then consumes provider-neutral candidates derived from those observations. Real closure evidence must use at least two independently selectable real webpage Worker resources/sessions and must demonstrate different Mission assignments. Prefer two genuinely different providers if Reality supplies them; **do not claim a second provider merely because the generic site adapter exists**. If the available environment exposes only one verified provider, the Phase remains open until a second real resource/provider boundary is honestly proven or the owning Cognition receives evidence requiring a scoped plan revision.

**Phase 8 boundary:** Phase 7 may mechanically match explicit required flags already present in `WorkerDescriptor.capabilities` and explicit model/provider/kind constraints. It does not infer capabilities from task semantics, choose tools/skills, pack mission-specific context, build token budgets, install a Skill Registry, route capability schemas or implement general context compatibility scoring. Those are Phase 8 concerns. `required imageInput = true → reject imageInput = false` is Phase 7; “this research probably needs vision/web/search so load these skills” is not.

**Durable ownership analysis:** no new durable owner is currently justified. `ProjectStore` remains Project/governance owner; `TaskRuntime` already durably records actual Worker attachment/retirement and execution/delivery state; `WorkerSessionManager` remains active Worker lifecycle/router owner; collaboration and Coordinator owners remain unchanged. Candidate inventories and health are ephemeral Reality observations. Assignment Request/Result are explicit operating inputs/results and reconstructible from caller intent plus current durable Mission/Worker history. Do **not** add `worker-pool-v1.jsonl`, `assignment-queue-v1.jsonl`, `scheduler-v1.jsonl` or mirror Mission membership. If Practice produces a concrete crash/restart case where safety/idempotency cannot be reconstructed from existing Task Worker history plus an explicit reissued request, return that evidence before proposing one minimal immutable assignment-intent fact.

**Canonical E2E:** owning Cognition explicitly defines Mission A and bounded hard/soft Worker requirements → assignment service enumerates current candidates → rejects wrong kind/provider/model/capability/health candidates → chooses a deterministic healthy Web candidate A → lazily creates and binds one disposable WorkerSession to Mission A → exact `managedSessionId` enters existing Phase 6 Coordinator delivery → A returns bounded Finding/Evidence, not transcript → owning Cognition explicitly defines Practice Mission B with different requirements → assignment selects a different admissible real Web resource B → exact Coordinator route sends the Work Order → B acts through existing capability boundary and raises durable Problem → Coordinator returns the Problem without auto-routing → Cognition explicitly decides feedback route → selected Cognition Worker answers through verified Phase 4/6 semantics → same Practice Mission B continues. Assignment automation never decides that A or B should exist.

**Replacement E2E:** unfinished Mission M + explicit Assignment Request → Worker A candidate selected/bound → A later becomes verifiably unusable/session-lost/rate-limited after its current turn boundary settles → M remains active → old Worker lifecycle is retired/detached according to known state → durable Task executions/delivery state are inspected and no UNKNOWN input is auto-replayed → same bounded request (or an explicitly revised request) is reevaluated → Worker B is selected and bound to the **same Mission M** → bounded Context Handoff/durable facts reconstruct current work → a newly explicit Coordinator input continues M. No Mission M2 and no old provider transcript.

**Adversarial E2E / contract areas:** unavailable/offline candidate cannot be selected; stale descriptor availability cannot override fresh resource health; degraded resource is not automatically preferred/selected; missing required capability/model/provider fails closed; forbidden provider/local-only constraint is never weakened; soft preference cannot outrank a hard constraint; wrong Project/root/Mission assignment fails; finalized/finalizing Mission rejects assignment; concurrent initial assignment cannot create unintended duplicate sessions; a provider-native identity retired by durable Mission/Worker history cannot be reused; unrelated Missions cannot share one disposable session; session creation success + binding failure cannot silently publish a routable orphan; ambiguous binding persistence cannot trigger speculative fallback; Worker death before first send can replace safely; known post-turn failure does not imply replay; UNKNOWN/pending execution or delivery cannot cause replacement + resend; page refresh/session-generation loss does not kill Mission; replacement continues the same taskId; Coordinator still requires exact managedSessionId and never becomes selector; selector does not invent Mission requirements or semantic “best model” scores; Web page/DOM details stay below candidate source/transport; Phase 8 context/skill routing does not leak in; no candidate cache becomes Project memory or permanent scheduler brain.

**Known risks:** treating one dynamic Web descriptor as two providers; moving page/DOM/site heuristics into the Worker selector; making `WorkerSessionManager` choose resources and thereby mixing policy with lifecycle ownership; persisting a scheduler/outbox merely for convenience; silently weakening explicit user/privacy constraints when preferred resources fail; ranking “smartest model” from semantic task content; using a stale `available` descriptor as live truth; racing create/bind so multiple sessions become current; retrying after uncertain Task persistence; replacing a Worker and replaying an UNKNOWN side effect; carrying provider transcript into replacement; keeping long-lived cross-Mission web conversations for pool efficiency; changing Phase 6 exact-command semantics to accept fuzzy provider expressions; prematurely implementing Phase 8 capability/context routing.

**Prohibited scope:** no Mission creation/decomposition/goal/plane/type/completion decisions in assignment; no autonomous Coordinator provider choice; no permanent background scheduler brain; no cross-Mission disposable session reuse; no provider transcript memory; no cost/latency/quality inference without a typed evidence-backed contract; no TaskMissionMetadata resource-policy expansion without restart evidence; no new assignment/pool journal by default; no Web DOM selector or page token in generic assignment contract; no Phase 8 Skill/Context/Capability Router; no Phase 9 broad UI; no Proposal D/Phase 10 Project Formation; no autonomous Human Confirmation/Commit behavior.

Cognition will directly inspect and independently reproduce high-risk filtering/concurrency/UNKNOWN/replacement cases after each Work Order. Existing Worker/Task/Context/Coordinator/WebMCP suites remain regression gates. #### Phase 7 Practice Work Order #1 — Provider-neutral assignment contract + deterministic safety core

**Status: AUTHORIZED / DISPATCHED by the active Phase 7 Cognition Mission (2026-09-15).** Use one persistent **Phase 7 Practice — Worker Assignment Core** Mission. Do not create a new Practice Mission for individual contract questions, test failures or ordinary repairs. Return `RESULT / PROBLEM / IMPLEMENTED / EVIDENCE / COGNITION RECONCILIATION NOTES / HANDOFF` to this same Phase 7 Cognition Mission and wait; do not self-authorize WO#2, real-provider closure, Independent Verification or Phase 8.

**Historical purpose:** implement the smallest provider-neutral mechanical seam that can assign already-authorized Mission work to an admissible Worker resource while proving in code that assignment is neither Mission planning nor Worker lifecycle ownership. This Work Order establishes the generic safety contract only. It does **not** yet claim the historical “two real Web AIs” proof; that remains the next Web-specific slice after Cognition reconciliation.

**Required production shape:**

1. Add one small Nimora-owned Assignment Request/Candidate/Result contract plus one stateless/reconstructible assignment service above `WorkerSessionManager` (preferred narrow locations/names such as `src/worker-assignment.ts` are acceptable but not mandatory). The service may depend on `TaskRuntime`, `WorkerSessionManager` and injected candidate sources. It must own **no durable journal, queue, Project memory, background loop, provider transcript or semantic Mission state**.
2. Bind every request to exact `projectId + rootMissionId + missionId`. Before selection, validate the current Task snapshot is a Mission in that exact Project/root and is not terminal. Do not infer or create Mission goal/plane/type/completion criteria. The actual bind remains linearized by existing Manager→TaskRuntime `createSession(..., missionId)` / `attachWorkerSession()` ownership so a concurrent finalization still fails closed at the owner boundary.
3. Keep `TaskMissionMetadata` unchanged in WO#1. Assignment requirements/preferences are bounded request data. Do not add provider/model/cost/latency/privacy policy to immutable Mission metadata and do not create an assignment-intent journal.
4. Define a provider-neutral candidate shape sufficient for mechanical eligibility: bounded `candidateId`, exact registered `workerId`, provider, Worker kind, observed availability, advertised models, implemented Worker capabilities and observation/health identity needed to refresh the same candidate. Do not put Web page ids, DOM selectors, page tokens, site-specific login state or provider transcript content into the generic contract.
5. Define a narrow injected candidate-source seam that can enumerate candidates, freshly re-observe/revalidate an exact candidate and materialize the exact adapter `WorkerSessionOptions` needed by `WorkerSessionManager.createSession()`. The selector may treat those materialized options as opaque. Candidate sources do not get Mission-planning authority and do not own session lifecycle after Manager creation.
6. Implement hard-constraint filtering before ranking. WO#1 must support at least: allowed Worker kind(s), allowed provider(s), forbidden provider(s), exact required model when supplied, and explicit required capability flags already represented by `WorkerCapabilities`. Hard constraints never weaken when no resource matches. Unknown/unsupported requirement keys fail closed rather than being ignored.
7. Implement soft preference ranking only over hard-admissible candidates. Support explicit provider order and model order where supplied; then use stable deterministic `candidateId` tie-breaking. Do not infer “best/smartest/cheapest/fastest” from task text, labels or extensions. Cost/latency scoring is outside WO#1.
8. Availability is two-stage evidence, not a boolean constant. Initial candidate observation may filter obvious `unavailable`; the candidate actually selected for creation must be freshly revalidated. WO#1 automatic assignment admits only `available + healthy` candidates. `degraded`, `unavailable`, `offline`, missing-health or stale/unrefreshable selected candidates are not auto-selected in this slice.
9. Selection does not call `send()`. After one candidate is selected, the service may only materialize options and ask the existing Manager to create/bind one session. A candidate that becomes explicitly unavailable **before any session/turn is admitted** may be skipped in favor of the next already-admissible candidate. An arbitrary create/bind exception or persistence ambiguity is **not** blanket fallback authority: fail closed or reread durable Task/Manager state as needed; never speculatively create another session when it is unknown whether the first binding became authoritative.
10. Serialize/recheck automatic **initial assignment** per Mission with a small in-memory operation lane or equivalent reconstructible critical section, not a scheduler. Two concurrent calls for the same Mission must not publish two unintended live sessions. If a Mission already has an active bound WorkerSession and the service cannot prove it is the one compatible current assignment, fail closed rather than silently taking over/rebinding it. Do not solve this by making `WorkerSessionManager` globally “one session per Task”; existing lower-level semantics remain broader for replacement/history/manual callers.
11. Assignment Result must return exact selected `candidateId / workerId / provider / model? / managedSessionId / missionId` (or an equivalently bounded provider-neutral projection) so a later host/Coordinator route can use the exact `managedSessionId`. The Result itself is not Project truth and is not a delivery acknowledgement.
12. Do not modify Phase 6 exact-command semantics to accept provider queries or requirements. Do not add automatic Coordinator assignment, automatic Work Order send, replacement/replay behavior, WebMCP page discovery, production extension composition or real-provider E2E in WO#1. Those are later evidence-gated slices.

**Mandatory adversarial proof:**

- wrong Project/root/Mission request rejects before resource creation;
- finalized Mission rejects; a finalization race still cannot publish a late Task Worker binding because the existing owner gate wins;
- missing required capability, unsupported exact model, forbidden provider and unavailable/offline candidate are filtered out;
- hard constraints outrank every soft preference, including a preferred forbidden provider;
- two equally admissible candidates select deterministically regardless of enumeration order;
- stale initially-available candidate that refreshes unhealthy/unavailable is not selected;
- degraded candidate is not auto-selected even when it is the only remaining resource;
- candidate that becomes explicitly unavailable before create may fall through to the next admissible candidate without sending any Mission input;
- arbitrary/ambiguous create-or-bind failure does not blindly create another WorkerSession;
- concurrent same-Mission initial assignment produces at most one new active binding, with the loser/retry returning/rejecting deterministically rather than creating a second session;
- an existing unrelated Mission's WorkerSession is never rebound/reused for the new Mission;
- selector/service exposes no `send`, Mission creation, semantic completion, feedback routing, Commit or capability-routing authority;
- no assignment/pool/scheduler journal is created and `TaskMissionMetadata` remains unchanged.

Practice should explicitly report whether any create/bind persistence ambiguity cannot be safely classified with the present Manager API instead of papering over it.

#### Phase 7 Cognition reconciliation — WO#1 Practice Result #1 (2026-09-15)

**Verdict: WO#1 NOT YET ACCEPTED — REPAIR REQUIRED.** Practice's own focused smoke and all required regression/type/compile gates pass, but Cognition independently reread the implementation and ran disposable falsification probes that reproduced three hard-boundary defects not covered by the Practice smoke. These findings are repository Reality learned by Cognition; they are not a rejection of the overall assignment architecture and do not authorize WO#2.

**P7-WO1-R1 — explicit empty hard allowlists are silently weakened.** `hardConstraintsMatch()` currently guards `allowedKinds` / `allowedProviders` with `.length`, so an explicitly supplied empty allowlist is treated as if the constraint were absent. A Cognition-owned probe supplied `allowedProviders: []` and observed a successful Worker assignment. An explicit hard allowlist may not become unrestricted merely because it is empty. Repair may interpret an explicit empty allowlist as match-none or reject that request before resource observation, but it must fail closed and must not create a WorkerSession.

**P7-WO1-R2 — the authoritative bound session model can violate the selected / required model.** The service validates materialized `WorkerSessionOptions.model`, but after `WorkerSessionManager.createSession()` it trusts the adapter-returned handle model. A Cognition-owned fake adapter deliberately ignored requested `model-a` and returned `model-b`; the service still returned a successful Assignment Result with `model-b` under `requiredModel: model-a`. The hard model constraint must hold at the actual bound WorkerSession, not only at option materialization. A mismatch discovered after create/bind must never return success or trigger candidate fallback. Cleanup must go through existing Manager lifecycle ownership and leave no active current assignment; any cleanup/persistence uncertainty remains fail-closed rather than becoming retry authority.

**P7-WO1-R3 — registered Worker-definition availability is not freshly revalidated.** The service checks the Manager's cached registration descriptor before ranking, but does not refresh the exact Worker definition before create. **Project-level authorization (2026-09-16): `Phase 8 AUTHORIZED / Phase 8 Cognition AUTHORIZED / Phase 8 Practice NOT YET AUTHORIZED`.** Project-level Cognition / 总文 independently absorbed the Phase 7 terminal closure, confirmed the fresh verifier `PASS`, no remaining Phase 7 Practice Work Order, unchanged branch/HEAD and the current Context/Capability source baseline. One fresh **Phase 8 Cognition / Architecture Mission** is authorized to reconstruct current Reality, reconcile the older Context/Skill routing design against Mission Work semantics and persist a Phase 8 Mission Plan. It must not implement production code or create a Phase 8 Practice Mission before that plan exists and an explicit bounded Work Order is issued. Phase 9 remains unauthorized.

**Authority rule:** Phase 8 Cognition owns understanding, architecture, decomposition, Work Orders, Reality reconciliation, verification readiness and semantic completion for this Phase. It does not execute its own Practice Work Orders. After issuing the first Work Order it must produce a separate Practice launch prompt and enter `WAITING_FOR_PRACTICE_RESULT`; a user message such as “continue” never escalates Cognition into Practice authority.

### Historical mission

Prevent context and tool-schema growth after the Mission semantics are stable.

This phase should absorb/align with the existing migration plan's Context / Skill Dynamic Routing work.

### Work

- mission-type-aware context budgets;
- compact capability catalog + dynamic schemas;
- Skill Registry;
- cognition/practice specific skill loading;
- bounded Finding/Problem/Answer/Handoff compression;
- stale Project/Mission fact invalidation;
- Context Inspector metrics.

### Phase 8 Cognition starting scope

The starting problem is **selective materialization**, not a rewrite of the Task/Worker/Assignment stack. Phase 8 Cognition must first map current source and decide the smallest composable boundaries for:

- a Mission-aware Context Engine that selects bounded Project/Mission facts, decisions, evidence, artifacts and Handoff material under explicit budgets without provider transcript inheritance;
- a compact Capability Catalog / Router that consumes the existing `capability-registry.ts` semantic identities and materializes only relevant executable schemas, without taking execution/policy/provider ownership;
- a Nimora Skill Registry / selector that treats skills as bounded instruction/workflow knowledge rather than executable tools and reuses platform/provider skill facilities only through adapters where appropriate;
- mission-plane/type-aware profiles for Cognition vs Practice without hard-coding one permanent agent class per role;
- explicit stale-fact / supersession handling derived from durable Project/Mission/Decision/Collaboration truth instead of heuristic deletion of history;
- measurable Context Inspector outputs such as selected/omitted sections, budget use, capability-schema count and compression/truncation reasons.

Phase 8 Cognition must inspect `src/context-handoff.ts`, `src/capability-registry.ts`, Task context/grant/execution contracts, current host capability execution/policy seams, Worker input/adapters, Mission collaboration exchanges, Project Decision routing and existing AgentHost/Codex skill infrastructure before choosing any new owner or schema.

### Preserved upstream boundaries

Phase 8 must consume, not weaken, the independently verified Phase 6/7 laws:

- Project ≠ Mission ≠ WorkerSession; Worker ≠ Mission; Coordinator ≠ Cognition;
- Phase 7 assignment remains mechanical explicit constraint/resource matching and keeps exact Project/root/Mission scope, hard constraints, fresh definition/resource validation, one stable Web Worker definition with exact Web target/session lineage, same-Mission replacement and UNKNOWN/no blind replay;
- Phase 6 Coordinator composition continues to receive exact `managedSessionId`; Context/Capability routing must not turn that exact execution identity back into a fuzzy provider selector;
- Problem transport remains inert until explicit Cognition routing; no Context Engine may infer and auto-create feedback Missions from provider output;
- Context Handoff remains provider-neutral; provider transcript, raw reasoning, page DOM/session tokens and provider-native conversation state are not Project/Mission memory;
- Bridge/Gateway/WebMCP remain transport/capability infrastructure, not Context/Project brains.

### Initial non-goals

- no Phase 9 Project/Mission UI implementation beyond bounded diagnostics/metrics needed to verify Context selection;
- no Phase 10 Project Formation or Proposal D implementation;
- no rewrite of Phase 7 Worker assignment/ranking or Web resource identity;
- no Mission planning inside Capability/Skill routers or Coordinator;
- no new Project/Mission membership owner, transcript store, global vector-memory brain or provider-specific DOM knowledge in generic context contracts;
- no unified Policy Engine rewrite unless a narrow Phase 8 routing contract demonstrably requires an adapter to already-existing approval/grant semantics;
- no automatic side-effect retry or weakening of execution/delivery uncertainty laws;
- no claim that Core AgentHost/Codex skill facilities already constitute the Nimora Skill Registry merely because platform skill APIs exist.

### Practice authorization gate

Phase 8 Practice remains unauthorized until Phase 8 Cognition has directly read current source/tests and persisted a `PHASE MISSION PLAN` that at minimum defines: context sources and authority ordering; budget model; stale/superseded fact semantics; capability catalog/materialization boundary; skill identity/trust/source model; Cognition-vs-Practice profile semantics; Worker/Coordinator/Assignment composition; restart/replay expectations; canonical/adversarial E2E; planned bounded Work Orders; prohibited scope; and verification strategy. Only then may Cognition issue WO#1 and launch one persistent Phase 8 Practice Mission. Fresh comprehensive Independent Verification remains the expected closure gate because context/tool exposure changes can alter execution authority even when no owner migration is intended.

### Current durable PHASE MISSION PLAN — 2026-09-16

**Phase:** Mission Work Phase 8 — Mission-aware Context / Skill / Capability routing.

**Historical goal:** prevent Project/Mission continuity from degenerating into ever-growing prompts, permanent provider conversations or “give every Worker every tool” once Mission semantics are stable. For an **already-defined Mission** and an **already-selected exact Worker**, materialize only the bounded Project/Mission truth, workflow knowledge and executable capability schemas relevant to that Mission/turn. Phase 8 is selective materialization; it is not Mission planning, Worker selection or a new Project memory owner.

**Current repository Reality:** branch/HEAD remain `main` / `79ab464acd0eac9eb623e2f6df2a1276088ece19`, with the intentional cumulative Phase 1–7 dirty tree preserved. Phase 7 is independently CLOSED / COMPLETE and all 43 current `test-shuncode-*` suites passed at its terminal verification boundary. Phase 8 Cognition has fresh-read the current architecture docs, ADRs, Context Handoff, Capability Registry, Task Runtime/grants/executions, Worker contract/adapters, Phase 7 assignment service, host capability policy/execution seams, Mission collaboration store, Project governance/Decision routing, Phase 6 Coordinator input/live service and AgentHost/Codex/Copilot/Claude skill/customization facilities. A focused Phase 8 baseline rerun of `test-shuncode-context-handoff`, `test-shuncode-capabilities`, `test-shuncode-capability-grants`, `test-shuncode-host-capability-policy`, `test-shuncode-mission-collaboration`, `test-shuncode-project-decision`, `test-shuncode-worker-assignment` and `test-shuncode-mission-coordinator-live` is green.

The existing substrate is intentionally split. `src/context-handoff.ts` already provides a provider-neutral, restart-reconstructible Task/Mission package with bounded todos/artifacts/executions/Worker history, a hard character budget and explicit truncation reporting; it does not include provider transcript contents or `adapterSessionId`. Its weakness for Phase 8 is not correctness but a relatively fixed package, recency/item-limit policy and section order. `src/capability-registry.ts` already binds stable semantic capability metadata to concrete tool names and explicitly leaves schemas/implementations to providers; it is not a Mission-aware router. `WorkerInput` already has `allowedCapabilities` plus concrete `externalCapabilities`, but those fields are transport inputs rather than approval/execution ownership. Current file/IDE registries own concrete schemas. Platform AgentHost facilities already discover/project skills from multiple provider conventions and sources, but those facilities expose provider/platform customization identity and lifecycle, not Nimora Mission relevance, trust policy, capability requirements or context-cost semantics. There is no existing Nimora Skill Registry or Mission-aware Context/Capability router to preserve.

The older `MIGRATION_PLAN.md` “Phase 10 — Context / Skill Dynamic Routing” is therefore consumed as **historical capability intent**, not as current Phase numbering or a Task-only architecture. Its prerequisite — stable Capability Registry + Task Runtime + Worker Contract — is now satisfied and sits below the independently verified Mission/Coordinator/Assignment chain. Current Mission Work Phase 8 owns this work under the newer Project/Mission semantics.

**Verified upstream invariants:** Project ≠ Mission ≠ WorkerSession; Worker ≠ Mission; provider conversation ≠ Mission identity. ProjectStore remains Project/governance owner; TaskRuntime remains Mission/work/grant/execution/artifact/Handoff owner; MissionCollaborationStore remains bounded relation/exchange owner; WorkerSessionManager remains exact active Worker lifecycle/router owner. Cognition decides meaning/decomposition/semantic routes. Phase 7 assignment mechanically binds an already-authorized Mission to an exact Worker and returns exact `managedSessionId`; Phase 8 must consume that result, never choose a substitute. Phase 6 Coordinator transports exact already-authorized routes and remains non-planning. Capability visibility, capability approval/grant, execution, result delivery and retry are distinct authorities. UNKNOWN execution/delivery is current safety truth, never inferred success and never replay authority. Full provider transcript/raw reasoning/page DOM/page tokens/provider-native conversation state remain non-authoritative and excluded from continuity.

**Context authority and authoritative input set:** one Phase 8 materialization request is scoped to exact `projectId + rootMissionId + missionId + managedSessionId` and is reconstructed from current owners rather than from transcript memory. The authoritative inputs are:

1. current Project snapshot and applicable **Committed** Project Decisions from `ProjectStore`; draft/proposed/unconfirmed governance is not current Project truth;
2. current exact Mission/Task snapshot from `TaskRuntime`: Mission identity/plane/type/completion criteria, goal, bounded Task context, progress/todos, artifacts, Worker history, grants and exact execution/delivery states;
3. typed Mission relations/exchanges from `MissionCollaborationStore`, restricted to the target Project/Mission relevance graph and preserving Finding/Problem/Evidence/Answer/Handoff identity/provenance;
4. the already-selected exact Worker definition/session from Phase 7/`WorkerSessionManager`, used only for compatibility/materialization, not provider choice;
5. explicit Cognition/host-authored materialization constraints for this turn, including required context items/categories, profile overrides and hard budget limits;
6. `capability-registry.ts` semantic metadata plus narrow adapters to the existing provider/tool schema owners;
7. narrow skill-source adapters over current Nimora/project/platform/provider-effective skill facilities.

No raw provider transcript, hidden old chat retrieval, provider reasoning, site DOM, page/session token or provider-native session identifier may be admitted as Mission knowledge merely because an adapter can read it.

**Authority is not recency and selection priority is not semantic truth:** normative Project authority comes from current committed governance; current Mission work state comes from the exact Task snapshot; typed collaboration exchanges are bounded evidence/coordination facts and do not silently become Project governance. Under budget pressure, Phase 8 uses deterministic selection tiers rather than “newest text wins”:

- **Tier 0 — non-omittable identity/safety:** exact Project/root/Mission/Worker route, active/finalized state, completion criteria needed for the turn, explicit Cognition hard constraints, UNKNOWN/pending execution or delivery facts whose omission could authorize unsafe action, and materialization incompatibility notices;
- **Tier 1 — current authority/current work truth:** applicable committed Project Decisions, current Mission goal/constraints/current Task context, and the current routed Problem/Answer/Handoff continuity required for the turn;
- **Tier 2 — directly supporting Reality:** evidence/artifacts referenced by Tier 1 facts, current task-relevant Findings/Evidence and relevant execution summaries;
- **Tier 3 — useful working context:** selected todos/progress/relevant files/history and other bounded contextual facts;
- **Tier 4 — optional enrichment:** additional research evidence/hypotheses/history explicitly useful to the chosen Cognition profile but not required for safe action.

An Answer to a current routed Problem can outrank an unrelated older Finding because it is explicitly connected to the active route; that does **not** mean age made the Finding stale. Evidence referenced by an authoritative/current item inherits the selection importance needed to understand that item. If Tier 0/required Tier 1 cannot fit, materialization must fail with a bounded budget incompatibility instead of silently truncating the safety/authority fact.

**Stale / superseded truth semantics:** `old != stale`. “Stale” is an exclusion result backed by explicit current authority/provenance, not timestamp age. Phase 8 may exclude or demote a fact as stale only when an existing owner proves that its applicability ended, for example: a Project Proposal is durably superseded; current Task fields replace older journal revisions of the same current-state field; a Worker-specific fact refers only to a detached/retired Worker when selecting active Worker context; a revoked grant must not be portrayed as current approval; a finalized Mission cannot receive new working-context admission; or another explicit contract proves replacement/supersession. The current Project governance schema does **not** provide a generic Committed-Decision-supersedes-Committed-Decision relation, so the router may not discard an older committed Decision merely because a newer Decision exists. If two committed Decisions appear applicable and conflict is not resolvable from explicit scope/provenance, preserve the ambiguity for Cognition rather than inventing a winner. Mission `supersedes` relations likewise do not automatically invalidate every individual fact produced by the older Mission.

**Context materialization model / smallest owner:** add a small Nimora-owned, provider-neutral **Mission Context Materializer** adjacent to the Task Runtime / Context Engine boundary. It is a read/derive service, not a new durable store. It validates exact scope and current Mission/Worker admissibility, gathers current authoritative snapshots, applies a deterministic Mission context profile and budget, returns a structured materialization package plus inspector record, then renders/adapts the selected result into existing bounded Worker-input/Context-Handoff seams. `context-handoff.ts` remains the proven provider-neutral replacement-continuity substrate; Phase 8 should compose/evolve it rather than delete it merely to rename the layer. A later contract version is allowed only when Practice proves the richer structured package cannot be represented safely through the current seam.

The core selector should be deterministic and provenance-based in v1. Embeddings/vector retrieval or an LLM summarizer may later be explored as ranking/compression aids, but they must never silently manufacture authority, hide omitted current truth or become the sole Project memory. No global vector-memory brain is authorized in Phase 8.

**Minimal Context Budget model:** retain a provider-neutral character/accounting model for v1 because current Worker descriptors do not expose one stable cross-provider context-window/token contract. Do not invent exact token capacity from model names. A materialization request/profile carries one hard input budget plus bounded section envelopes for at least `instructions`, `decisions/current-truth`, `evidence`, `artifacts`, `history/handoff`, `skills`, and `tool-schemas`, plus an `output-reserve` field when the caller/adapter has an explicit capacity contract. If output capacity is unknown, inspector state must say the reserve is unspecified; the router must not pretend it has protected N provider tokens. Future provider adapters may translate known provider capacity into this neutral budget through a narrow adapter without moving context ownership into the provider.

Section envelopes are not rigid equal percentages. Each profile defines minimum/non-omittable classes, caps and relative selection priority. Unused optional budget may flow to another eligible section, but mandatory current truth cannot be displaced by optional skills/tool schemas/history. Budget accounting includes rendered text and selected skill/schema payload costs, not only “context prose”.

**Compression / truncation model:** prefer deterministic structural compression over blind string slicing: select fewer bounded items; use stable ids/titles/summaries already owned by Project/Task/collaboration contracts; include references to artifacts instead of copying large content unless explicitly required; and preserve exact execution `status + deliveryStatus`. Existing source contracts already bound most text. Any dropped/shortened section records `selected / omitted / reason / original count or cost / materialized cost`. Safety/current-authority sections are item-atomic in v1: if a required item itself cannot fit, fail closed rather than slice it into misleading prose. Existing `renderContextHandoff()` hard character enforcement remains a final containment guard, but Phase 8 must arrange inputs so it does not become the first place critical facts are silently cut.

**Mission-aware context profile:** profiles are data-driven routing policy, not permanent “Cognition Agent” / “Practice Agent” classes. Profile resolution consumes `mission.plane`, `missionType`, exact Worker capabilities/compatibility and explicit Cognition-authored constraints. Plane/type provide defaults; explicit hard constraints refine them; Worker capability facts may remove impossible materializations but may not select a different Worker.

- cognition/research-oriented defaults may allocate more evidence/history budget, admit explicitly relevant competing hypotheses as **non-authoritative** material, and prefer read/research skills/capabilities;
- practice-oriented defaults prioritize current committed decisions/constraints, the active Work Order/current Problem/Answer, task-relevant evidence and only the executable capability schemas/skills needed for Reality work;
- coordination remains a narrow transport/execution profile and does not inherit Cognition semantic context merely because it can move commands.

Mission type may further specialize these defaults (verification, repair, research, implementation, deliberation, etc.) without creating a model/provider class hierarchy. No profile may increase semantic authority beyond the sources it materializes.

**Capability Catalog identity:** the existing `CAPABILITY_METADATA_BY_TOOL` / `CapabilityMetadata.id` registry remains the sole Nimora semantic identity layer. Phase 8 may derive a compact catalog entry from existing metadata (`id/version/title/category/tags/environment/risk/idempotency/retry/approval/destructive/openWorld` plus a bounded implementation locator such as the already-registered tool name), but must not copy those semantics into a second router registry. Catalog selection is “what the Worker can be told exists”, not approval.

**Capability schema-materialization boundary:** concrete JSON schemas remain owned by current tool/provider registries (`file-tool-registry.ts`, `ide-tool-definitions.ts`, future MCP/adapter schema sources). A narrow schema-source adapter must map a selected semantic capability back to exactly one compatible concrete tool definition for the exact already-selected Worker/environment and verify that semantic capability id/tool identity/schema identity have not drifted. Only then can it populate the existing `WorkerInput.allowedCapabilities` / `externalCapabilities` projection. The router never calls the tool.

`tool visible != tool approved != tool executed`. Capability exposure requires known semantic metadata and a known execution/policy route; it does not create a Task grant. Existing `HostCapabilityPolicyAuthorizer`, Task/session grant resolver, execution coordinator/ledger, provider executor, result-delivery and retry/UNKNOWN laws stay authoritative. A capability whose approval semantics require a grant may be visible if the existing approval flow is intentionally capable of obtaining that grant, but the Context/Capability router must report the grant/approval state accurately and must not present visibility as pre-approval. No router path may convert schema selection into automatic retry authority.

**Worker compatibility / Phase 7 composition:** Phase 8 starts only after Phase 7 has produced an exact Assignment Result / `managedSessionId`. Context/Skill/Capability materialization validates that exact Worker against required input/tool/skill representation. If the selected Worker lacks required capability-request support, schema transport, image/context feature or another explicit hard materialization requirement, return a bounded incompatibility/Problem to owning Cognition/assignment authority. **Do not call the Phase 7 selector or silently bind a different provider/session inside Phase 8.** Same-Mission Worker replacement repeats Phase 7 assignment first, then freshly rematerializes Phase 8 context for the replacement Worker.

**Phase 6 Coordinator composition:** Phase 8 produces the bounded provider-neutral Worker-input material that an already-authorized Phase 6 route carries to the exact `managedSessionId`. Coordinator does not ask the router to infer a Mission, choose a provider, decide which Problem deserves Cognition or invent a capability set. Existing exact Coordinator semantic-command schemas remain exact. Phase 8 may provide a materialized context package/skill/tool projection as host-prepared input to the command, but the Coordinator remains a bridge/executor.

**Skill identity / source / trust model:** Skill remains instruction/workflow knowledge, never executable authority. Phase 8 should introduce a small **Nimora Skill Index/selector** whose records normalize only routing metadata needed above providers: stable Nimora skill id + version/digest, title/description, source kind + source locator/provenance, trust classification, enabled state, trigger/relevance tags, relevant Mission planes/types, required semantic capability ids, estimated context cost and content materializer. The Skill record may refer to an existing provider/platform skill; it does not own that provider's lifecycle or make provider-native ids Project truth.

Existing AgentHost/Codex/Copilot/Claude customization facilities should be reused through source adapters where useful. They already expose URI/path/name/description, containers/scopes, enablement/load state and in some cases plugin version/provider-effective catalog state. They do **not** by themselves establish a Nimora trust decision or Mission relevance contract. The Nimora layer must therefore distinguish source provenance from trust. First-party/built-in or explicitly accepted project/workspace sources can be auto-eligible under narrow policy; third-party/plugin/provider-only sources whose trust cannot be established are excluded from automatic loading or require explicit caller/user trust. An untrusted skill may never silently override committed Project truth, Mission constraints or tool approval semantics. This conservative default resolves Phase 8 start without a new product-value decision; any future desire to auto-trust third-party skills across projects is a separate security/user-control deliberation.

Skills may declare **required semantic capabilities** only as prerequisites/relevance facts. Loading a Skill does not grant, expose or execute those capabilities. Skill selection must fail or omit with an explicit reason if its required capabilities cannot be represented under the exact Worker/profile/policy boundary.

**Restart / replay / replacement semantics:** no new `context-routing-v1.jsonl`, Skill-selection journal, capability-routing journal or prompt transcript store is justified by current Reality. Project Decisions, Task/Mission state, collaboration facts, artifacts, grants/executions and Worker history are already durable under their owners; capability/skill catalogs are reconstructible observations; materialization request/profile is explicit operating input. After restart, re-read owners and rematerialize. A replacement Worker receives bounded current truth and Handoff, not the old provider transcript. If Practice demonstrates a concrete crash/restart safety case that cannot be reconstructed from these inputs, it must return `PROBLEM + EVIDENCE` before adding the smallest new immutable fact.

Provider adapter checkpoints may continue to exist as adapter-owned opaque continuity mechanics under the existing Worker contract, but they are not promoted into Project/Mission semantic context and cannot substitute for durable Mission truth.

**Finalized Mission rule:** a finalized/finalizing Mission does not receive a new working materialization or executable tool exposure. Historical/archive inspection may read already-durable facts through read-only inspection surfaces, but that is not a new Worker work admission. This preserves Phase 2/6/7 finalization linearization.

**Context Inspector metrics:** every materialization attempt should produce a bounded structured inspection record suitable for tests/debugging without creating Phase 9 UI ownership. #### Phase 8 Cognition reconciliation — Repair WO#1A Practice Result (2026-09-16)

**Verdict: Repair WO#1A NOT YET ACCEPTED — one further bounded normalization repair is required.** Practice correctly closed the originally reproduced JSON-shaped P8-WO1-R1 cases and P8-WO1-R2: string booleans, unsupported profiles, unknown section keys and unsupported nested fields now return structured `invalid-request`; related research inside the explicit bounded relevance universe remains absent from Practice Worker text but is visible as `profile-excluded`; an explicitly required bounded related item can be promoted without widening its peers; and derived `parent_of` relations no longer independently admit every child Mission's research corpus. The same fresh probe then falsified the stronger **strict runtime normalization** claim on a non-JSON host-object shape. `exactKeys()` inspects only own enumerable keys, while normalization subsequently reads properties through ordinary prototype lookup. Cognition observed the target Practice Mission widen from `related research excluded` to `related research included`. A second normalization-only probe also showed that a sparse `requiredItemIds = Array(1)` passes normalization into semantic owner access because `Array.prototype.map()` preserves the hole instead of validating one bounded non-empty id. These are the same fail-open family: runtime shape validation is not yet an exact own-value schema boundary.

**P8-WO1A-R1 — inherited/sparse runtime values can bypass exact request normalization.** This is blocking for WO#1 because the materializer is explicitly a host/runtime boundary whose hard profile constraints determine information exposure. It is not sufficient that `JSON.parse()` normally creates plain objects; production callers are TypeScript/JavaScript host code and the WO#1A contract explicitly required runtime authority rather than trusting static shapes. A malformed object must not widen context merely because a policy field lives on its prototype, and a sparse array must not defer malformed-id detection until after semantic owner access.

Therefore the current API Worker can accept a dynamic schema **shape**, yet that fact alone does not establish an executable/policy route for every schema source. WO#2 currently has no per-tool/source compatibility check and can expose a schema whose current exact Worker route is absent.

It does not execute its own Practice Work Orders.
