#### Required liveness authority

While the exact active WebMCP Worker turn is `running` and the host is canonically polling that exact input, a valid provider tool request must remain discoverable even if:

```text
finite response burst
= exhausted

MutationObserver wake
= absent
```

Preferred minimal layering:

```text
canonical workerPoll(exact inputId)
→ if exact active turn is still running:
   drive/await one current-page scan pass
→ refresh turn
→ return snapshot
```

An equivalent lifecycle-bound design is acceptable only if it provides the same deterministic guarantee without adding a competing perpetual scanner.

Do not solve R11 merely by extending 10 seconds to a larger finite number. A larger finite burst leaves the same correctness hole.

Do not make manual `window.__shuncodeWebMcp.scan()` a required external action.

#### Poll semantic boundary

Poll-driven scan is allowed to **discover/admit** provider output that already exists for the exact active turn.

It must not:

```text
resend provider input
create a second Worker turn
manufacture tool calls
re-run already-seen calls
re-run a side effect after delivery uncertainty
bypass host-managed capability routing
```

For host-managed turns:

```text
late exact allowed capability
→ capability_call event exactly once
→ pendingHostCapabilities exactly one
→ page-local invoke count 0
```

The host remains the only executor.

For ordinary page-local WebMCP turns, existing invocation semantics remain unchanged and dedupe must still guarantee one invocation per call occurrence.

#### Dedupe / concurrency invariants

Existing `call-occurrence-v2` remains authoritative.

Repeated or concurrent polls must not duplicate an admitted call:

```text
same rendered call occurrence
+ N workerPoll calls
→ one handleCall admission
→ one capability_call event
→ one host pending-capability identity
→ at most one page-local invocation when page-local mode applies
```

Current `busy / scanRequestedWhileBusy` serialization must remain coherent.

If multiple polls overlap:

```text
scan execution
= serialized

duplicate semantic execution
= 0
```

#### Terminal / cancellation boundary

Poll liveness applies only to the exact current `running` turn.

After:

```text
completed
cancelled
error
interrupt convergence
disconnect
```

later poll/health activity must not admit a new tool request for that terminal turn.

An interrupt racing with poll-driven observation must preserve WO#1I:

```text
no Manager idle while provider running
no post-cancel capability admission
no replay
exact input ownership
canonical convergence
```

#### Pending delivery boundary

Existing result-delivery retry rules remain unchanged:

```text
delivery failure
→ retry result delivery only
→ never re-run original tool/capability side effect
```

Poll-driven scans must respect pending deliveries and current seen/dedupe state.

#### Required occurrence identity invariant

Occurrence identity must no longer depend solely on the number of same-id calls that remain in the current DOM.

Required:

```text
same logical rendered provider call
+ repeated scan / poll / DOM refresh
→ same occurrence identity
→ execute/admit at most once

genuinely later provider call
+ same explicit provider call id
+ older call virtualized out
→ different occurrence identity
→ admissible exactly once
```

The provider's explicit `call.id` remains the protocol id used for host result routing.

The internal dedupe occurrence identity may be richer than the provider call id.

Preferred repair direction:

```text
DeepSeek stable message/item identity
+ call position within that logical message
+ provider baseKey / call id
→ stable internal occurrence identity
```

This allows the same provider id in two different assistant messages to remain distinct even if only one message is currently mounted.

For an exact host-managed Worker turn, a turn-local message-order fence may also be used so only provider messages belonging to the new turn are eligible. Do not assume a generic numeric ordering unless the DeepSeek adapter validates it.

If the required stable DeepSeek message identity is absent or ambiguous for a host-managed turn, fail closed rather than silently falling back to the unsafe current-DOM ordinal.

An alternative design is acceptable only if deterministic tests prove the same invariants.

Historical v2 persisted keys must not be allowed to suppress a genuinely new stable-identity occurrence merely because its provider id is reused.

Do not solve R12 by clearing all persisted seen state.

#### Production repair

`webmcp-site-adapters.js` now exposes three bounded DeepSeek-only observations:

```text
assistantMessageIdentity(element)
assistantMessageOrder(element)
conversationItemBoundary()
```

The stable identity is derived only when the assistant candidate has exactly one `data-virtual-list-item-key` ancestor within the bounded ancestor walk and that value is a canonical non-negative safe integer. The identity is `deepseek-item:<key>`; its numeric value supplies the bounded ordering evidence. Multiple matching ancestors, malformed/non-numeric values, or unsafe values are not guessed.

For a host-managed DeepSeek Worker turn, `workerSend()` captures the current maximum valid virtual-list item order before provider send as that exact turn's historical floor. Invalid boundary state fails before provider send:

```text
missing / malformed / ambiguous ordering
→ fail closed
→ no provider send
→ no capability admission
→ no page-local invoke
```

`toolCallOccurrences()` retains the provider call unchanged but now gives a stable DeepSeek occurrence an internal key equivalent to:

```text
deepseek-message:<stable logical message identity>
::call:<position within that message>
::provider:<provider baseKey / call.id>
```

The exact encoding is implementation-owned. It is not exposed as provider protocol authority. Generic/non-DeepSeek behavior retains the existing current-DOM ordinal key.

Current-turn DeepSeek admission now requires:

```text
stable message identity/order
AND
messageOrder > exact pre-send turn floor
```

Therefore:

```text
same logical message + DOM replacement/rerender
→ same internal occurrence identity
→ no replay

historical virtualized message re-enters DOM
→ order <= turn floor OR already-seen stable identity
→ no replay

new logical message after send
+ same explicit provider call.id
→ new stable occurrence identity
→ eligible exactly once
```

At repaired runtime injection, current visible historical stable DeepSeek occurrences at/below the injection floor are seeded into the existing persisted `seen` set. Existing v2 `id::occurrence:N` entries are retained. Practice does not clear Session Storage, clear `seen`, or delete historical replay protection.

#### Provider callId/result-routing preservation

The dedicated R12 regression exposed one additional manifestation of the same occurrence-identity collision before the repair was complete. After two genuinely different stable logical messages reused the same provider `call.id`, capability admission could occur twice correctly, but the pre-repair host-result bookkeeping keyed delivered results only by:

```text
provider callId + capability name
```

so the second logical occurrence's result could be mistaken for the first occurrence's already-delivered result.

Practice repaired that inside the same WO#1L boundary by separating internal occurrence/result identity from provider routing:

```text
provider route
= exact original callId + capability name + active inputId

internal pending/result identity
= exact stable occurrence identity
```

One unresolved provider route maps to one stable occurrence at a time. A later same-id logical occurrence is not marked seen while the earlier identical provider route is unresolved; after the earlier result resolves, the later occurrence can be admitted and resolved exactly once. `workerResolveCapability` still receives/routes the exact original provider `callId`, capability name and inputId, and `sendToolResult` still returns the original provider call id/name. Internal dedupe identity never replaces provider protocol identity.

#### Blocking falsification: ambiguous result acknowledgement plus later provider-route reuse

Candidate #2 still has one result-routing ambiguity inside the existing R12 boundary.

The page runtime now has a stable internal logical-occurrence identity, but the provider result route exposed to host control remains inputId + original callId + capability name. WorkerSessionManager retains an outstanding host-requested result by inputId + callId, with capability name validated on that pending entry.

If page/provider result submission succeeds but the success acknowledgement is lost, or the adapter/transport call throws after provider acceptance, WorkerSessionManager intentionally retains the old pending entry so result delivery can be retried without reexecuting the capability. That retry authority is correct and must remain safe.

The uncovered failure occurs when the provider continues and a later logical assistant occurrence reuses the same provider call.id + capability name before the old Manager-side delivery outcome is known.

Cognition reproduced this twice without modifying production source.

Disposable current-source composed-page probe:

- occurrence #1 provider result was accepted;
- the upper acknowledgement was modeled as lost;
- later logical occurrence #2 reused the same provider callId + capability;
- retrying the old result #1 was consumed by occurrence #2;
- result #1 tool-result submissions = 2;
- intended result #2 tool-result submissions = 0.

The page route map had already advanced the reused callId + name to occurrence #2 and therefore could no longer distinguish an old occurrence #1 result retry from the new occurrence #2 result.

A second disposable probe bundled the exact current WorkerSessionManager and simulated the same acknowledgement-loss boundary:

- first Manager result submit caused provider acceptance of RESULT_ONE, then the adapter reported an error / lost acknowledgement;
- Manager retained the old inputId + callId pending identity;
- the same admitted send emitted logical occurrence #2 with the same callId and capability;
- current Manager admitted that second call while the old result-delivery identity remained pending;
- Manager's canonical retry sent RESULT_ONE again and settled the later waiter;
- the later intended RESULT_TWO was rejected as having no outstanding host-requested capability call;
- adapter-observed payloads = [RESULT_ONE, RESULT_ONE].

Therefore the page probe did not rely on an impossible caller action. The current Manager contract itself preserves exactly that old retry authority after an uncertain result-delivery acknowledgement.

This violates the required WO#1L invariant: sequential logical occurrences that reuse one provider call.id must each resolve their own exact logical occurrence exactly once, with no cross-occurrence result consumption.

The semantic capability side effect itself is not replayed by these probes. The defect is narrower: result-delivery authority for occurrence N can be consumed by occurrence N+1 after provider-route reuse.

#### Bounded continuation contract — SAME persistent Phase 11 Practice Mission

Practice must repair only the cross-occurrence result-routing ambiguity:

1. An ambiguous/failed acknowledgement for result delivery belonging to stable logical occurrence N must retain retry authority only for occurrence N.
2. A later logical occurrence N+1 that reuses the same provider call.id + capability name must never consume a retry belonging to N.
3. If a later same-route occurrence cannot be distinguished while N's result-delivery acknowledgement remains unresolved, fail closed or fence that route instead of cross-routing the old result.
4. The internal host/transport path may carry stable occurrence authority or use an equivalent exact fence. Provider-visible inputId, original call.id and capability name must remain unchanged where the provider protocol requires them.
5. Result-delivery retry must remain a retry of the already-computed result only. It must not reexecute the original capability or semantic side effect.
6. Ordinary sequential same-id logical occurrences must still each resolve exactly once after the preceding occurrence's result-delivery identity is safely settled.
7. Do not add a durable queue, outbox, scheduler or provider-transcript authority merely to solve this seam.

Permanent regression required:

logical occurrence #1 -> host capability executes once -> page/provider accepts result #1 -> result-delivery acknowledgement to Manager is lost/throws -> logical occurrence #2 reuses the same provider callId + capability -> canonical result #1 retry.

Required proof: result #1 retry settles only occurrence #1 idempotently; cross-occurrence consumption = 0; occurrence #2 cannot be falsely settled by result #1; correct result #2 resolves occurrence #2 exactly once when/if occurrence #2 is validly admitted; capability reexecution = 0.

The permanent regression must exercise the real current WorkerSessionManager -> WebWorkerAdapter/WebMCP transport -> page-runtime result-routing identity contract, or an equivalently exact deterministic seam. A page-only happy-path test is insufficient.

#### Accepted problem — P11-WO1-R13

```text
P11-WO1-R13
= After an exact WebMCP Worker send reaches browser-accepted "sent",
   a running turn with no subsequent observable provider progress has
   no autonomous bounded convergence owner.

Current behavior
= WebMcpCommandTransport continues canonical polling while snapshot.state
   remains "running".

Page behavior
= workerPoll() scans and refreshes the exact running turn but has no
   no-progress / provider-response deadline.

Consequence
= an external/provider/browser no-response condition can leave the
   production Worker turn running indefinitely until an outside actor
   explicitly interrupts it.
```

This defect is valid regardless of which external component caused the original no-response. A production autonomous Worker boundary must not require a human/Practice operator to discover that a sent turn has made no observable progress forever and manually terminate it.

The `006` final `cancelled` state is **not** evidence that production spontaneously cancelled the turn. Roadmap evidence shows Practice explicitly invoked the existing canonical:

only after the exact turn remained running with zero assistant/tool output for roughly seven minutes. #### Exact Repair surface

Production repair is intentionally confined to:

- `extensions/shuncode/src/webmcp-worker-transport.ts`

Permanent deterministic coverage is added in:

- `scripts/shuncode-webmcp-no-progress-convergence-smoke.mts`;

#### Deadline / progress ownership

`WebMcpCommandTransport` now owns a finite configurable no-progress deadline:

```text
production default
= 300000 ms

deterministic regression injection
= 25 ms
```

The inactivity clock begins only after the exact
`_shuncode.webMcp.workerSend` call has returned from the page runtime. The
page `workerSend` return is after its accepted browser-send boundary, so a
pre-send wait cannot consume the provider inactivity budget.

The deadline refreshes only on real turn progress:

- assistant-text event / changed response text;
- a newly admitted capability-call event / increased tool-call count;
- capability-result progress, including host result received/delivered state;
- capability rejection is also terminally meaningful provider/tool progress
  for the admitted turn.

These are deliberately **not** progress:

- `workerPoll()` by itself;
- `scan()` by itself;
- `lastScanAt` advancement;
- arbitrary status/observation churn such as a fresh scan-observed event.

Before timing out, the transport performs at least one post-send canonical
poll so output that arrived near the boundary still receives a normal
observation opportunity.

#### Exact convergence / terminal semantics

After the configured inactivity interval expires while the exact input is
still running:

1. the transport requests the exact current `workerInterrupt(inputId)`;

#### Consolidated R14 continuation contract

The submit owner must prove one candidate that is simultaneously **associated, rendered/actionable, effectively enabled, semantically non-conflicting, unique, and identity-stable** before consuming the provider gesture key.

Association: if the composer is in a form, submit authority is limited to that exact form. If there is no exact repository/live-evidenced container relationship, fail closed; do not fall back to scanning all document buttons. If current DeepSeek genuinely has a no-form composer, Practice may use fresh read-only DOM evidence to define one narrow structural owner/container, but must not use global page search or proximity ranking.

Rendered/actionable: do not treat layout-box existence alone as visible. At minimum reject hidden/display-none/visibility-hidden/collapsed, aria-hidden/inert controls, zero-visible-render cases and controls that cannot receive the intended user action. `opacity:0` and `pointer-events:none` must not become provider submit authority. Prefer one fixed bounded actionability predicate rather than browser-wide heuristics.

Effectively enabled: do not rely only on `button.disabled`. Reject native `:disabled` state including disabled fieldset inheritance, `aria-disabled=true`, inert/non-interactive state, and any fixed current-provider disabled semantic supported by evidence. A control legitimately disabled while composer is empty may be preflight-identified only if it becomes effectively enabled after fill and remains the same exact identity; no gesture key is consumed until then.

Semantic precedence: compute one authoritative semantic identity, not "any field matches". A non-empty higher-priority accessible name such as `aria-label="Message settings"` must not be overridden by `title="Send"` or text `Send`. Conflicting semantic sources fail closed unless a fixed provider-specific rule proves which source is authoritative. Exact allowlist remains bounded; no broad substring/fuzzy match.

Uniqueness and identity: zero or multiple associated/actionable/effectively-enabled admissible controls fail before gesture. Re-resolve after fill and require the same DOM/control identity plus the same authoritative semantic identity and association. Identity/actionability/enabled drift fails before gesture.

Current `observeProviderUserAdmission()` immediately rejects the first observation with more than one new provider-user identity. R16 therefore requires a **bounded admission stabilization protocol**, not relaxed admission. Transient multi-identity / role ambiguity must remain pending within the existing bounded provider-admission observation window. Admission may be credited only when exactly one new stable provider-user identity with exact full outbound text and exact current conversation lineage is established under a stable observation. A stably persistent true multiple-user/double-send condition must still fail closed. #### R16-B — host-managed occurrences require exact provider admission

Current global MutationObserver/scan can handle a host-managed occurrence while `activeWorkerTurn.state=running` even though `sentAt=0` and provider-user admission is still pending. WO#1P must add an **admitted-turn occurrence gate**. For a host-managed Worker turn, post-floor occurrences discovered while provider admission is pending must be quarantined/deferred: do not `rememberSeen`, increment `toolCallCount`, emit `capability_call`, invoke generic Bridge, create pending delivery, or send a tool result. If the same turn later obtains exact provider-user admission, those same occurrences may be rescanned under the now-admitted host-managed turn and routed exactly once. #### R16-C — failed host-managed occurrences must not fall through to generic Bridge

013's rendered `Unknown Bridge tool: nimora.coordinator.deliverExplicitMissionInput` is classified as secondary fallout from the same missing occurrence-ownership gate, not evidence that the Coordinator capability is unregistered. The capability is canonically owned by `mission-coordinator-worker-input.ts` / `MissionCoordinatorLiveDriver`. Once admission failure changes the Worker turn from running to error, current global no-argument MutationObserver `scan()` loses the host-managed current-turn context and a later post-floor tool block can fall through to generic `invokeTool()`.

They must not generate `Unknown Bridge tool`, generic capability side effects, pending tool-result delivery, or a provider tool-result gesture. Quarantine must be exact to the failed turn/page/conversation floor and must not disable ordinary generic WebMCP outside that scope. A future exact Worker turn establishes a fresh floor/authority.

#### Cognition source falsification

Current production command:

~~~text

~~~

is implemented as:

~~~text
webWorkerSessions.listSessions({
  workerId: "nimora.web-worker"
})
~~~

Therefore it enumerates the DeepSeek/WebMCP Worker class only and cannot prove that a:

~~~text
nimora.chatgpt-browser-worker
~~~

managed session is absent.

Separately, current ChatGPT controller resource discovery intentionally does:

~~~text
if (pageIsOwned(page.pageId))

~~~

and probeResource returns undefined for an owned page.

Therefore:

~~~text
exact Target absent from chatgptWorker.listResources
or
chatgptWorker.probeResource = undefined
~~~

does **not** mean the exact connected Target is dead.

It is the expected assignment-candidate behavior while that page is already owned.

## 16. Canonical acceptance scenario

Use one real but bounded project as the recurring E2E acceptance case. A personal blog is appropriate.

Scenario A:

```text
Project: Personal Blog
Root Mission: Add music player
Research Mission: investigate existing solutions
Practice Mission: implement selected solution
Practice raises mobile compatibility Problem
New Cognition Mission investigates it
Answer returns to Practice
Practice completes
Independent Verification Mission validates behavior
Root Coordinator completes and retires
```

Scenario B must begin later with a fresh root/coordinator:

```text
New Root Mission: Add synchronized lyrics
```

Pass condition: Scenario B succeeds using Project state + relevant handoffs/current code, without reviving or requiring the full transcripts from Scenario A.

## 17. Per-phase AI Mission protocol

Every Sol chat implementing this roadmap receives:

1. Project Constitution (`AGENTS.md`, architecture docs, ADR 0001-0003);
2. exactly one phase/mission brief;
3. relevant Research Capsule/Handoff only;
4. explicit completion criteria and prohibited scope;
5. requirement to emit `PROBLEM` when assumptions fail instead of silently expanding scope;
6. requirement to update architecture docs/ADR when ownership/contracts change;
7. requirement to produce a final Handoff only when the assigned Mission actually reaches a terminal boundary;
8. requirement to respect routing authority at handoff: an in-Phase successor prompt is allowed only when the current role owns that in-Phase routing; a Phase-closing worker must hand control back upward rather than generating an authoritative next-Phase prompt.

### Mission termination gate

A chat does **not** hand off merely because work remains. If the assigned Mission can still be advanced safely in the current chat, the Worker must continue the same Mission.

Terminal output (`RESULT`, final `HANDOFF`, and when authorized an in-scope `NEXT MISSION`) is allowed only when at least one of these is true:

- the Mission's own completion criteria have been satisfied;
- a Verifier has completed the full planned audit and can issue its terminal PASS/FAIL judgment;
- a real external blocker prevents useful further progress in this Mission;
- the current Worker/session can no longer continue reliably because of a genuine tool/context/runtime limitation.

A discovered in-scope defect, a failing test, unfinished checklist work, or the simple fact that more work remains is **not** a handoff boundary. `INCOMPLETE` is a forced-terminal state, not a synonym for "I still have work to do". When the current chat can continue, it should continue instead of creating a continuation Mission.

For Verifiers specifically, finding a failure does not end the Verification Mission. Continue auditing the remaining exit criteria whenever technically possible, then return one consolidated terminal judgment. Verifiers must not turn themselves into the Repair worker; implementation fixes belong to the subsequent consolidated Repair Mission unless the Verification brief explicitly authorizes a tiny diagnostic-only test change.
### Hard phase-closure rule

`Implementation completed` is **not** equivalent to `Phase completed`.

For every implementation-bearing phase, the phase may be marked `CLOSED` only after a **fresh independent Verification Mission returns PASS** against the phase exit criteria, current repository state, tests and relevant invariants.

Independent verification is fresh for independence, but verification must be **consolidated rather than fragmented**. A verifier should audit the entire phase against all exit criteria and continue looking for additional defects after finding the first one whenever the repository remains inspectable. Its FAIL report should batch all observed blocking findings into one repair brief. The subsequent Repair Mission should address that batch, then exactly one fresh Re-Verification should assess the repaired baseline. Do not spawn one verifier/repair pair per individual defect.

The handoff routing rule is mandatory:

```text
Research / Architecture
→ Implementation
→ Independent Verification
   ├─ PASS → Phase Cognition reconciliation → Phase CLOSED → Project-level Cognition
   │                                               ↓
   │                                      choose next Phase route
   ├─ FAIL → Phase Cognition consolidation → in-Phase Repair Work Order/Mission → fresh Independent Verification
   ├─ INCOMPLETE → continuation Mission in the same Phase
   └─ BLOCKED → targeted Cognition/Problem Mission in the same Phase
```

The persistent Phase Cognition / Practice pattern validated by Phases 3 and 4 is now the preferred generic default: ordinary Practice results return to the still-live Phase Cognition Mission; verifier `FAIL` returns the consolidated finding set to that Cognition Mission; Cognition normally issues one consolidated Repair **Work Order** to the same continuing Practice Mission when ownership is unchanged, followed by a fresh independent Re-Verification. A Phase Mission Plan may still override this when repository evidence justifies a different in-Phase structure.

Therefore:

- an Implementer/Practice worker cannot close a phase and must return Result/Problem/Evidence to the current Phase Cognition authority rather than choosing its own successor;
- only an independent verifier may authorize phase closure with `RESULT: PASS`;
- a verifier does not own the next Phase. After `PASS`, it returns its terminal verdict to the still-live Phase Cognition Mission (or Project-level Cognition if no Phase Cognition survives);
- Phase Cognition may record closure only after reconciling the fresh verifier `PASS`; it must then emit a Final Phase Handoff / `PROJECT COGNITION REPORT` to Project-level Cognition and stop exercising Phase authority;
- Project-level Cognition alone chooses and dispatches the next Phase Cognition Mission. A closing Phase may recommend the roadmap candidate but must not generate/dispatch an authoritative cross-Phase successor prompt unless Project-level Cognition explicitly delegated that exact action;
- if the current phase is incomplete, every next mission remains in the current phase until its exit criteria pass;
- elapsed time, token use, number of modified files or an implementer's confidence are never phase-completion criteria.

### Reusable Mission Prompt

```text
你现在是 Nimora 项目中的一次性 GPT-5.6 Sol Worker。

你的唯一历史使命是：<MISSION>。
完成该使命后，本聊天生命周期结束。不得主动继续下一个阶段。

开工前必须读取：
- AGENTS.md
- docs/architecture/README.md
- docs/architecture/MISSION_WORK_ARCHITECTURE.md
- docs/architecture/adr/0001-0003
- 与本 Mission 直接相关的当前源码、测试和架构文档
- 上一 Mission 的 Handoff / Research Capsule（如有）

原则：
- 当前代码和测试是实现事实；文档是长期设计依据；发现不一致必须明确报告。
- 不创建与 TaskRuntime / WorkerSessionManager / Worker Adapter 竞争的第二套 Runtime。
- 不把 Nimora 产品业务重新塞入 Code-OSS Chat Core。
- 不把 technical Bridge/Gateway 当作 Coordinator AI。
- Project 长期存在；Mission 有明确终点；WorkerSession 是可替换执行资源。
- Plan 不是最终真理；实践发现新事实时必须允许认知修正。
- 不复制完整旧聊天作为跨 Mission 状态。
- 不扩大当前 Mission 范围。
- 不因为经过了十几分钟、一个测试失败或一个小缺陷就主动结束当前聊天；只要仍是同一个历史使命，应在当前 Mission 内完成正常的修复与重测。
- 如果你是 Verifier，必须尽量完成对本 Phase 全部 Exit Criteria 的一次性审计并汇总所有已发现阻塞项；不要发现第一个问题就立即结束，从而制造“一问题一验证聊天”。
- 如果当前 Phase 已经使用超过 6 个聊天，先执行 Consolidation Gate：以仓库真实状态为准合并剩余问题，并优先形成一个集中 Repair 或一次完整 Re-Verification，而不是继续碎片化。

工作流程：
1. 先调查当前真实实现。
2. 给出本 Mission 的最小变更方案和验证方案。
3. 再修改代码。
4. 运行相关 typecheck/unit/runtime/E2E smoke。
5. 独立检查 diff 与架构边界。

如果实践发现前提错误、缺少资料或需要超出当前 Mission 的设计决定，请停止扩张并输出：

PROBLEM
- 当前使命：
- 原假设：
- 实际观察：
- 证据：
- 需要回答的问题：
- 是否阻塞：

使命完成时输出 HANDOFF：
- Mission / Status
- 完成内容
- 修改文件
- 关键架构决定
- 测试与结果
- 已知限制/风险
- 未解决问题
- 下一任 AI 必须知道什么

如果这是 **Phase Cognition 的 Phase-closing handoff**，还必须额外输出给 Project-level Cognition 的：

PROJECT COGNITION REPORT
- Phase / terminal status
- independently verified facts promoted
- architecture / ownership impact
- unresolved Project-level strategic cognition
- human decision status
- recommended downstream candidate（仅候选，不是已授权 successor）
- lessons about the Phase operating process that should alter future routing rules

只有当当前 Mission 已触发上述终止条件、确实准备结束本聊天时，最终终止回复才输出：

RESULT: PASS | FAIL | INCOMPLETE | BLOCKED

Routing output depends on authority:

- Practice / Implementer: return Result/Problem/Evidence to the current Phase Cognition. Do **not** choose Independent Verification or the next Phase yourself.
- Independent Verifier: return the consolidated terminal verdict/findings to the current Phase Cognition. Do **not** generate a next-Phase prompt.
- Phase Cognition before closure: may issue the next in-Phase Work Order / Mission when its persisted Phase Plan authorizes it.
- Phase Cognition after verifier `PASS`: close/reconcile the Phase, output Final Phase Handoff + `PROJECT COGNITION REPORT`, then return control to Project-level Cognition. You may name a downstream candidate but **must not** create or generate the authoritative prompt for the next Phase.
- Project-level Cognition: after repository reconciliation, may generate the next Phase Cognition prompt.
- `RESULT=INCOMPLETE` is only for a Worker that truly cannot continue its Mission; unfinished work alone is not a handoff boundary.
- `RESULT=BLOCKED` stays inside the current authority scope unless the blocker is genuinely Project-level.

完成后停止，不继续寻找新工作。
```

## 17. Independent verifier prompt rule

Verifier must be a fresh chat. Give it the Mission brief, relevant architecture docs, actual diff/current source and Implementer Handoff, but not the Implementer's full reasoning transcript.

The verifier owns the **independent phase-closure verdict**, not implementation or cross-Phase routing. It must end with an explicit `RESULT: PASS | FAIL | INCOMPLETE | BLOCKED`. Only `PASS` authorizes the Phase Cognition authority to record closure. A verifier must not prepare or dispatch the next Phase's Mission Prompt; its result returns to Phase Cognition for closure reconciliation, and cross-Phase control then returns to Project-level Cognition.

Its mission is to try to falsify completion:

- contract/lifecycle invariant violations;
- replay/restart compatibility;
- accidental permanent Agent state;
- hidden transcript dependency;
- blind side-effect retry;
- Core boundary regression;
- insufficient tests;
- stale docs.

## 18. Stop conditions

Do not proceed to later phases if the current invariant is not demonstrated by tests/E2E.

Especially stop if:

- completed workers can still silently migrate into unrelated missions;
- Mission state only works while a chat page remains open;
- a Practice Problem cannot survive restart/replay;
- deliberation draft text can mutate engineering state without commit;
- Coordinator becomes the only holder of Project truth;
- WebMCP site/DOM details leak into Mission contracts;
- context inheritance requires old full transcripts.

## 19. Definition of success

The architecture is proven when this is boring and reliable:

```text
old AI completes mission
→ handoff/state persists
→ old AI retires
→ fresh AI continues project

practice discovers reality contradicts plan
→ durable Problem
→ fresh cognition mission researches/thinks
→ bounded Answer updates practice
→ work continues

human optionally discusses direction
→ no engineering mutation during draft
→ explicit commit
→ only affected missions receive the decision
```

At that point Nimora is no longer organized around a permanent chat session. The Project owns continuity; Missions organize work; Workers are replaceable compute.
